 Movsar Evloev thinks UFC 333 fight with Alexander Volkanovski could be 1st UFC finish: ‘Why not?’
 Movsar Evloev could finally find a finish at UFC 333
 by Alexander K. Lee Oct 18, 2026, 1:00 PM UTC Facebook 
 Link 
 Movsar Evloev knows fans want to see him win a fight without the scorecards. He could make it happen against Alexander Volkanovski at UFC 333.
 This Saturday in Abu Dhabi, the undefeated Evloev makes the walk to the octagon for the biggest fight of his life as he challenges Volkanovski for the UFC featherweight title. Evloev is 20-0 as a pro, 10-0 since making his UFC debut in 2019, so it’s fair to say he’s earned his shot the hard way. One reason why it may have taken so long for the matchmakers to come around on Evloev is his lack of finishes, as he’s yet to score a knockout or submission in the promotion.
 UFC 333 would be the perfect time for his first.
 “Maybe my fighting style [made it take longer than I expected], but still the most important thing is still winning the fight,” Evloev told MMA Fighting’s José Youngs. “Now, I feel like I’m getting better and I’ve got more abilities to finish the fights and we were working on that since I won my last fight. Even before, it was always fun to finish opponents, but I had tough opponents. None of them is easy to finish. Even just to win them is already a big deal, right?
 “Now, maybe my first finish in my first title fight, why not? I have everything to do that.”
 Evloev has also been plagued by bouts of inactivity, but when fight night rolls around, he’s delivered, scoring victories over numerous ranked opponents. His past four wins have come against Lerone Murphy, Aljamain Sterling, Arnold Allen, and Diego Lopes, the latter of whom went on to leapfrog Evloev and meet Volkanovski in a pair of title fights.
 That success has kept Evloev in the UFC’s good graces, even without a standout highlight reel, which can’t be said for some notable departures in the past few years, including the undefeated Farid Basharat, who was recently allowed to walk despite a 16-0 record. Evloev was asked for his thoughts on quality fighters not being kept on the roster, and he believes winning still matters.
 “I have zero finishes in the UFC, but I’m still in UFC and I’m fighting for the title, so that means that not just finishes is important,” Evloev said. “To show a good fight is also important. Even if you have no finishes, you can show good fight, exciting fight. You can show the beauty of wrestling and there is not just fans of MMA who just wait for blood and something crazy, there are so many good fans who know MMA and they understand and maybe because of them I’m still in the UFC.”
 Volkanovski has suggested Evloev’s wrestling won’t be enough to beat him, and that the challenger will eventually have to throw down if he hopes to dethrone the two-time champion. For now, Evloev isn’t taking the bait, and he’s planning to stay the course with tactics that have paid major dividends so far.
 Tactics that might just lead to him taking Volkanovski out inside the distance anyway.
 “I have a responsibility,” Evloev said. “My whole republic, my whole country waiting for me to bring that title. OK, so for me, all of this is more important than just my ego, so maybe I will take the belt and then we will play around, like taking risks or something.”
 “Even if I knock him out, not because my wrestling doesn’t work, but because it works very good, so I will make him tired,” he added. “Then, when I feel, OK we can knock him out, then I will try and knock him out. But he’s saying he will take my confidence. Nobody can.”
